Burn rate is how fast, relative to the SLO, the error budget is spent; burn rate 1 exhausts it exactly at the window's end.
A fixed-duration threshold gives the same detection time to a severe and a mild incident, and can keep firing long after the incident ends.

items.item: A short window at roughly 1/12 the long window clears the alert soon after the problem does, fixing the reset-time failure.

at.step: Reveal: the recommended thresholds — and their limit

items.item: A fixed age threshold for freshness pages every night on a table that is supposed to look old right before its scheduled run; measuring against the expected schedule instead fixes it, and this is this topic's own addition, not sourced from the workbook.
Deduplicating alerts from one upstream failure into one page, routed by ownership, prevents one real incident from paging many people for the same cause.
"Every page should be actionable" is the SRE book's own stated principle, with a real cost (triage time, missed real incidents) when alerting ignores it.
Topic 1's freshness metric and golden signals are the base this topic turns into an alert.
